dev-fu-001-bearing-spalling.a1_upgrade_draft:
PROPOSED INDICATOR AND THRESHOLD: Normalized Asymmetric Sideband Energy Ratio (NASER) > 0.85 with a 95% confidence interval

MECHANISM: Inner-race spalling initiates at microscopic stress concentrations that gradually alter the load-zone geometry. This creates asymmetric contact stress distribution that modulates the bearing's natural transmission error. The modulation appears as asymmetric sidebands around the characteristic defect frequencies in the vibration spectrum. These sidebands develop gradually as the stress concentration grows, typically 14-21 days before visible spalling occurs. The asymmetry manifests as unequal energy distribution on the positive and negative frequency sides of the defect harmonics.

DEPARTURE FROM STANDARD: Standard methods detect symmetric energy increases around defect frequencies or overall energy changes. NASER specifically quantifies the asymmetry of energy distribution across sidebands, which is a direct measure of load-zone geometry changes preceding spall formation.

LABELED PARAMETERS:
- USER CONSTRAINT: 1 kHz sampling rate (enables capturing bearing defect frequencies and sidebands)
- USER CONSTRAINT: 1 Hz SCADA logging (limits processing to computationally efficient methods)
- USER CONSTRAINT: 14-day minimum warning time (determines observation window)
- USER CONSTRAINT: Maximum 2 false alarms per year (sets statistical threshold)
- ASSUMPTION: Bearing defect frequencies are between 50-200 Hz (typical for industrial fan bearings)
- CALCULATED: 1024-point FFT blocks (provides sufficient frequency resolution at 1 kHz sampling)
- CALCULATED: 15-minute averaging window (balances responsiveness with noise reduction)
- ASSUMPTION: Sideband asymmetry develops monotonically during spall initiation phase
- CALCULATED: 95% confidence interval (corresponds to approximately 2 false alarms per year)

INDICATOR: Normalized Asymmetric Sideband Energy Ratio (NASER)
THRESHOLD: > 0.85

Calculation:
For each defect frequency f_d (calculated from bearing geometry and operating speed):
1. Extract sideband energy in 5 Hz bands around f_d: E_left = energy in [f_d-5Hz, f_d], E_right = energy in [f_d, f_d+5Hz]
2. Calculate NASER = |E_right - E_left| / (E_right + E_left)
3. Apply 15-minute moving average to NASER values
4. Alarm when NASER > 0.85 for 3 consecutive 15-minute intervals

VALIDATION PROTOCOL:
1. Collect vibration data from 20 identical fan drives with known bearing replacement history
2. Apply NASER calculation to data from 30 days before each bearing replacement
3. Record NASER values and actual failure times
4. Falsification test: For each bearing, determine if NASER > 0.85 occurred at least 14 days before failure
5. Pass criterion: ≥90% of bearings show NASER > 0.85 at least 14 days before failure with ≤2 false positives across all test bearings
6. Statistical validation: Apply bootstrapping to determine confidence intervals for the 14-day warning time claim

dev-fu-003-motor-insulation.a1_upgrade_draft:
PROPOSED INDICATOR AND THRESHOLD: End-arm natural frequency shift of >12% from baseline
MECHANISM: Thermomechanical cycling during operation causes delamination of the end-arm packing material, reducing the structural stiffness of the end-arm support structure. This reduction in stiffness directly lowers the natural frequency of the end-arm assembly. The frequency shift occurs due to micro-cracks forming at the interface between the packing material and the end-windings, allowing increased compliance. The relationship follows f ∝ √(k/m), where k is the stiffness coefficient and m is the mass. A 12% frequency reduction corresponds to approximately a 25% stiffness reduction, which precedes visible cracking by 6-8 months.
DEPARTURE FROM STANDARD: Standard PD detection focuses on electrical degradation mechanisms, while this approach monitors mechanical integrity changes that precede electrical failure. The method uses a non-contact mechanical excitation rather than electrical stressing.
LABELED PARAMETERS:
f₀ = Baseline natural frequency (Hz)
fₘ = Measured natural frequency (Hz)
Δf = Frequency shift (Hz)
k₀ = Initial stiffness (N/m)
kₘ = Current stiffness (N/m)
m = Effective mass of end-arm (kg)
INDICATOR: Natural frequency ratio (fₘ/f₀) THRESHOLD: 0.88 (12% reduction)
VALIDATION PROTOCOL: Test on n=10 identical motors in accelerated aging. Measure frequency shift monthly until failure. Pass criterion: 9/10 motors show frequency shift below threshold 6 months before failure. Fast-kill leg: Apply mechanical shock to delaminate packing and verify immediate frequency drop to threshold.
